survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This policy brief uses ICCS 2016 grade eight data from the 14 European countries participating in the ICCS 2016 European module. The tolerance outcome is constructed from four grade-eight student questionnaire items on equal rights for immigrants, and civic knowledge is taken from the ICCS 2016 civic knowledge test with proficiency levels (A and above vs C and below). Analyses are described as performed with IEA’s IDB Analyzer using the Regression option, which indicates use of ICCS’s complex survey design features in the tool, but the brief does not report the specific student weight variable name or whether replicate weights were used. Because the brief is not an ML prediction study and does not report model training, it does not discuss ML-specific weighting omissions; instead, it reports associations and standardized regression coefficients from the IDB Analyzer output.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variable in this brief is an attitude scale score based on questionnaire items (tolerance toward immigrants), not a cognitive achievement score represented by ICCS/PISA-style plausible values. As a result, plausible-value handling is not applicable to the reported tolerance scale comparisons. The brief also does not document any missing-data strategy (e.g., listwise deletion or imputation), so missing-data handling is treated as a reporting gap for transparency.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analyses use ICCS 2016 grade eight student data from the 14 European countries participating in the ICCS 2016 European module. The tolerance outcome is based on students’ responses to four questionnaire items about equal rights for immigrants (with reverse-coded items as indicated), and civic knowledge is categorized using ICCS 2016 proficiency levels (focus on students at or above level A and at or below level C). The brief does not report additional exclusions (e.g., missing item responses, incomplete questionnaires) or any further task/module restrictions beyond the European module and grade-eight scope.

data.outcome_summary: This IEA ICCS 2016 policy brief examines tolerance toward immigrants among grade eight students in 14 European educational systems. Tolerance is measured using four questionnaire items on equal rights for immigrants, forming a scale comparable across countries (international mean 50, SD 10). The brief reports that students’ tolerance is, on average, relatively high across Europe but varies widely within and between countries, illustrated by differences between 5th and 95th percentiles and by country-specific gaps. It further shows that students with higher civic knowledge proficiency (level A and above) tend to be more tolerant than those at level C or below, and that civic knowledge has the strongest association with tolerance compared with gender, immigration status, and socioeconomic status. The brief emphasizes the cross-sectional nature of ICCS, so associations should not be interpreted causally.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a policy brief rather than an empirical machine-learning paper: it reports descriptive comparisons and regression-based associations using IEA’s IDB Analyzer, without training or evaluating ML models. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally empty. The brief also does not provide the final analytic sample size or per-country student counts, limiting extraction of total_students and n_students.
